messages:
Alice: CI job https://ci.redwood.internal/4807/job/4321 is red on `runtime_tests::memory_fence` — failing intermittently 2-3x out of 10 runs on macos-latest. can someone grab this? :grimacing:
Ben: Ack. Is there a minimal stack or log?
Alice: paste of failing snippet:
```
thread 'tests::memory_fence' panicked at 'assertion failed: val == expected', src/serve/fence.rs:214
stack backtrace:
  0: fence::check
  1: runtime::start
  2: tests::memory_fence
```
Carlos: Any recent changes touching fences or relaxed atomics in the last few commits?
Alice: Range is `a1b2c3d..f4e5g6h` — PR #842 changed some ordering in `kv/cache` but not fences explicitly.
Dina: Hypothesis: scheduler/crossbeam reordering under macos thread affinitization. Could be a timing window. Does the test use `std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed` anywhere?
Emma: Quick try: can you run locally with `RUST_TEST_THREADS=1` and `RUST_BACKTRACE=1`? Also try `ulimit -u` and `taskset` equivalent on mac to pin CPUs.
Alice: I ran `cargo test runtime_tests::memory_fence -- --nocapture` w/ `RUST_TEST_THREADS=1` and saw it pass 20/20. With parallel threads it failed 3/25.
Ben: That points to a race. Can we bisect to narrow the commit that regressed frequency? I'll volunteer to bisect if you give me the commit range.
Carlos: Also try ASAN/TSAN or MIRI? TSAN might help but test uses `unsafe` and low-level atomics so TSAN could be noisy. Still worth a debug run.
Dina: If the issue is timing dependent, a good short repro is to add a tight loop that starts N threads with randomized yield/nap between ops to amplify. Alice, can you add a small harness in `tests/repro/memory_fence_harness.rs` that spins the problematic pattern 500x?
Alice: I'll add a quick harness and push to my branch in ~30m. For CI I scheduled a rerun: https://ci.redwood.internal/4807/job/4321/rerun — ci-bot said rerun queued.
ci-bot: Rerun requested by Alice — job queued on macos-latest (shard 3).
Ben: While Alice is adding repro, I'll start a git bisect on the range and run with the harness locally. If I find a suspicious commit I'll post results here.
Emma: Another data point: I ran the test on linux (ubuntu-latest) and didn't see failures (0/100). Looks mac-specific, could be libstd scheduling behavior.
Carlos: Could also be the CI VM has different CPU count causing thread interleavings. Try setting `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=4` or forcing thread counts to match CI.
Alice: Pushed harness branch: `alice/memory-fence-harness`. Link: https://git.redwood/alice/runtime/compare. Harness fails locally in <1s when run in parallel.
Ben: Starting bisect. I'll post updates.
Ben: Found candidate commit `e7f9c2b` which touches `alloc::waiter` behavior — running more iterations to confirm.
Dina: If `alloc::waiter` changed a wake ordering, that could flip happens-before assumptions. Worth trying to revert locally to confirm.
Ben: Reverted `e7f9c2b` locally, harness passes 500x. Re-applied, fails within 50 runs. Looks like a regression. Filing a minimal PR to revert for testing.
Alice: Thanks Ben — can you open a bisect PR or at least a draft so CI can run full matrix?
Ben: Will open PR and request `eng-runtime` review. Marking as high priority: `labels: ci-red, flaky-test, bisect-in-progress`.
Emma: Also added a quick CI smoke: run harness on macos, linux, and dedicated low-cpu VM to reproduce across configurations.
Carlos: Action items: (1) Ben to open PR/revert candidate, (2) Alice to land harness under `tests/repro`, (3) Dina to review atomics usage in `alloc::waiter`, (4) Emma to run cross-OS smoke.
Alice: TL;DR: unstable mac scheduling exposed a regression in `e7f9c2b`. Ben is bisecting + opening PR, I've added a harness to make reruns cheap. Ping me if you want to join bisect or run harness locally. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: Job rerun completed: macos-latest shard 3 — failure reproduced (1/1).
Ben: PR opened: https://git.redwood/pulls/894 — requesting quick review from Dina and Carlos.
Dina: Reviewing now. If revert looks good we'll merge and then follow up with a proper fix to `alloc::waiter` ordering.
Emma: Noted. I'll update the flaky-test tracker and temporarily disable the test on macos CI with a skip tag if the revert lands (so nightly stability stays green).
Alice: Thanks everyone. I'll add the harness link to the ticket and close the loop once CI stabilizes.
